<div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;page-break-after:always;width:88.24%;border:0;margin:30pt 5.88% 30pt 5.88%;"></div><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:5.88%;padding-right:5.88%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><a id="GLOSSARYOFCERTAINDEFINITIONS_247371"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;text-align:center;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;text-decoration-color:#000000;">GLOSSARY OF CERTAIN DEFINITIONS</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; &#8220;our&#8221; or &#8220;ours&#8221; when used in this Annual Report on Form&#160;10-K refer to Whiting Petroleum Corporation, together with its consolidated subsidiaries. &#160;When the context requires, we refer to these entities separately.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We have included below the definitions for certain terms used in this Annual Report on Form&#160;10-K:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;ASC&#8221;</i> Accounting Standards Codification.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Bankruptcy Code&#8221; </i>Title 11 of the United States Code.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Bankruptcy Court&#8221; </i>United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Basis Swap&#8221; </i>A derivative instrument that guarantees a fixed price differential to NYMEX at a specified delivery point. &#160;We receive the difference between the floating market price differential and the fixed price differential from the counterparty if the floating market differential is greater than the fixed price differential for the hedged commodity. &#160;We pay the difference between the floating market price differential and the fixed price differential to the counterparty if the fixed price differential is greater than the floating market differential for the hedged commodity.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Bbl&#8221;</i> One stock tank barrel, or 42 U.S. gallons liquid volume, used in this report in reference to oil, NGLs and other liquid hydrocarbons.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Bcf&#8221;</i> One billion cubic feet, used in reference to natural gas.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;BOE&#8221; </i>One stock tank barrel of oil equivalent, computed on an approximate energy equivalent basis that one Bbl of crude oil equals six Mcf of natural gas and one Bbl of crude oil equals one Bbl of natural gas liquids.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Btu&#8221;</i> or <i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;British thermal unit&#8221;</i> The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of one pound of water one degree Fahrenheit.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;completion&#8221;</i> The process of preparing an oil and gas wellbore for production through the installation of permanent production equipment, as well as perforation and fracture stimulation to optimize production.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;costless collar&#8221; </i>An option position where the proceeds from the sale of a call option at its inception fund the purchase of a put option at its inception. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;deterministic method&#8221;</i> The method of estimating reserves or resources using a single value for each parameter (from the geoscience, engineering or economic data) in the reserves calculation.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;development well&#8221; </i>A well drilled within the proved area of an oil or natural gas reservoir to the depth of a stratigraphic horizon known to be productive.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;differential&#8221; </i>The difference between a benchmark price of oil and natural gas, such as the NYMEX crude oil spot price, and the wellhead price received.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;dry hole&#8221; or &#8220;dry well&#8221; </i>A well found to be incapable of producing either oil or gas in sufficient quantities to justify completion as an oil or gas well.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;EOR&#8221; </i>Enhanced oil recovery.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;exploratory well&#8221;</i> A well drilled to find a new field or to find a new reservoir in a field previously found to be productive of oil or natural gas in another reservoir.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;extension well&#8221;</i> A well drilled to extend the limits of a known reservoir.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;FASB&#8221;</i> Financial Accounting Standards Board.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;field&#8221; </i>An area consisting of a single reservoir or multiple reservoirs all grouped on or related to the same individual geological structural feature and/or stratigraphic condition. &#160;There may be two or more reservoirs in a field that are separated vertically by intervening impervious strata, or laterally by local geologic barriers, or both. &#160;Reservoirs that are associated by being in overlapping or adjacent fields may be treated as a single or common operational field. &#160;The geological terms &#8220;structural feature&#8221; and &#8220;stratigraphic condition&#8221; </p></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">4</p></div></div></div>
<div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;page-break-after:always;width:88.24%;border:0;margin:30pt 5.88% 30pt 5.88%;"></div><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:5.88%;padding-right:5.88%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">are intended to identify localized geological features as opposed to the broader terms of basins, trends, provinces, plays, areas of interest, etc.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;GAAP&#8221;</i> Generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;gross acres&#8221; or &#8220;gross wells&#8221; </i>The total acres or wells, as the case may be, in which a working interest is owned.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;ISDA&#8221;</i> International Swaps and Derivatives Association,&#160;Inc.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;lease operating expense&#8221; or &#8220;LOE&#8221;</i> The expenses of lifting oil or gas from a producing formation to the surface, constituting part of the current operating expenses of a working interest, and also including labor, superintendence, supplies, repairs, short-lived assets, maintenance, allocated overhead costs and other expenses incidental to production, but not including lease acquisition or drilling or completion expenses.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;LIBOR&#8221; </i>London interbank offered rate.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MBbl&#8221;</i> One thousand barrels of oil, NGLs or other liquid hydrocarbons.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MBbl/d&#8221; </i>One MBbl per day.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MBOE&#8221; </i>One thousand BOE.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MBOE/d&#8221;</i> One MBOE per day.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Mcf&#8221;</i> One thousand cubic feet, used in reference to natural gas.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MMBbl&#8221;</i> One million barrels of oil, NGLs or other liquid hydrocarbons.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MMBOE&#8221; </i>One million BOE.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MMBtu&#8221;</i> One million British Thermal Units, used in reference to natural gas.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MMcf&#8221;</i> One million cubic feet, used in reference to natural gas.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;MMcf/d&#8221;</i> One MMcf per day.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;net acres&#8221; </i>or <i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;net wells&#8221; </i>The sum of the fractional working interests owned in gross acres or wells, as the case may be.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;net production&#8221; </i>The total production attributable to our fractional working interest owned.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;NGL&#8221; </i>Natural gas liquid.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;NYMEX&#8221; </i>The New York Mercantile Exchange.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;PDNP&#8221;</i> Proved developed nonproducing reserves.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;PDP&#8221; </i>Proved developed producing reserves.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;plugging and abandonment&#8221;</i> Refers to the sealing off of fluids in the strata penetrated by a well so that the fluids from one stratum will not escape into another or to the surface. &#160;Regulations of most states legally require plugging of abandoned wells.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;pre-tax PV10%&#8221;</i> The present value of estimated future revenues to be generated from the production of proved reserves calculated in accordance with the guidelines of the SEC, net of estimated lease operating expense, transportation, gathering, compression and other expense, production taxes and future development costs, using costs as of the date of estimation without future escalation and using an average of the first-day-of-the-month price for each of the 12&#160;months within the fiscal&#160;year, without giving effect to non-property related expenses such as general and administrative expenses, debt service and depreciation, depletion and amortization, or federal income taxes and discounted using an annual discount rate of 10%. &#160;Pre-tax PV10% may be considered a non-GAAP financial measure as defined by the SEC. &#160;Refer to the footnote to the Proved Reserves table in Item&#160;1. &#8220;Business&#8221; of this Annual Report on Form&#160;10-K for more information.</p></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">5</p></div></div></div>

0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;probabilistic method&#8221; </i>The method of estimating reserves using the full range of values that could reasonably occur for each unknown parameter (from the geoscience and engineering data) to generate a full range of possible outcomes and their associated probabilities of occurrence. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;prospect&#8221; </i>A property on which indications of oil or gas have been identified based on available seismic and geological information.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;proved developed reserves&#8221; </i>Proved reserves that can be expected to be recovered through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared to the cost of a new well.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;proved reserves&#8221;</i> Those reserves which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible&#8212;from a given date forward, from known reservoirs and under existing economic conditions, operating methods and government regulations&#8212;prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. &#160;The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced, or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project, within a reasonable time.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The area of the reservoir considered as proved includes all of the following:</p><table governmental entities.</span></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:12pt;"></div><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Existing economic conditions include prices and costs at which economic producibility from a reservoir is to be determined. &#160;The price shall be the average price during the 12-month period before the ending date of the period covered by the report, determined as an unweighted arithmetic average of the first-day-of-the-month price for each&#160;month within such period, unless prices are defined by contractual arrangements, excluding escalations based upon future conditions.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;proved undeveloped reserves&#8221; or &#8220;PUDs&#8221; </i>Proved reserves that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage, or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion. &#160;Reserves on undrilled acreage shall be limited to those directly offsetting development spacing areas that are reasonably certain of production when drilled, unless evidence using reliable technology exists that establishes reasonable certainty of economic producibility at greater distances. &#160;Undrilled locations can be classified as having undeveloped reserves only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five&#160;years, unless specific circumstances justify a longer time. &#160;Under no circumstances shall estimates of proved undeveloped reserves be attributable to any acreage for which an application of fluid injection or other improved recovery technique is contemplated, unless such techniques have been proved effective by actual projects in the same reservoir or an analogous reservoir, or by other evidence using reliable technology establishing reasonable certainty.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;reasonable certainty&#8221;</i> If deterministic methods are used, reasonable certainty means a high degree of confidence that the quantities will be recovered. &#160;If probabilistic methods are used, there should be at least a 90&#160;percent probability that the quantities actually recovered will equal or exceed the estimate. &#160;A high degree of confidence exists if the quantity is much more likely to be achieved than not, and, as changes due to increased availability of geoscience (geological, geophysical and geochemical) engineering, and economic data are made to estimated ultimate recovery with time, reasonably certain estimated ultimate recovery is much more likely to increase or remain constant than to decrease.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;recompletion&#8221;</i> An operation whereby a completion in one zone is abandoned in order to attempt a completion in a different zone within the existing wellbore.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;reserves&#8221;</i> Estimated remaining quantities of oil and gas and related substances anticipated to be economically producible, as of a given date, by application of development projects to known accumulations. &#160;In addition, there must exist, or there must be a reasonable </p></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New <div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;page-break-after:always;width:88.24%;border:0;margin:30pt 5.88% 30pt 5.88%;"></div><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:5.88%;padding-right:5.88%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">expectation that there will exist, the legal right to produce or a revenue interest in the production, installed means of delivering oil and gas or related substances to market, and all permits and financing required to implement the project.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;reservoir&#8221;</i> A porous and permeable underground formation containing a natural accumulation of producible crude oil and/or natural gas that is confined by impermeable rock or water barriers and is individual and separate from other reservoirs.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;resource play&#8221; </i>An expansive contiguous geographical area with known accumulations of crude oil or natural gas reserves that has the potential to be developed uniformly with repeatable commercial success due to advancements in horizontal drilling and completion technologies.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;royalty&#8221; </i>The amount or fee paid to the owner of mineral rights, expressed as a&#160;percentage or fraction of gross income from crude oil or natural gas produced and sold, unencumbered by expenses relating to the drilling, completing or operating of the affected well.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;royalty interest&#8221;</i> An interest in an oil or natural gas property entitling the owner to shares of the crude oil or natural gas production free of costs of exploration, development and production operations.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;SEC&#8221; </i>The United States Securities and Exchange Commission.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows&#8221; </i>or <i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;Standardized Measure&#8221; </i>The discounted future net cash flows relating to proved reserves based on the average price during the 12-month period before the ending date of the period covered by the report, determined as an unweighted arithmetic average of the first-day-of-the-month price for each&#160;month within such period (unless prices are defined by contractual arrangements, excluding escalations based upon future conditions); current costs and statutory tax rates (to the extent applicable); and a 10% annual discount rate.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;turn-in-line&#8221; or &#8220;TIL&#8221; </i>To turn a drilled and completed well online to begin sales.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;working interest&#8221;</i> The interest in a crude oil and natural gas property (normally a leasehold interest) that gives the owner the right to drill, produce and conduct operations on the property and to a share of production, subject to all royalties, overriding royalties and other burdens and to all costs of exploration, development and operations and all associated risks.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">&#8220;workover&#8221; </i>Operations on a producing well to restore or increase production.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><span style="font-weight:bold;visibility:hidden;">&#8203;</span></p><a id="_a77406df_7728_48d0_ae5c_ed0a8b2233b3"></a></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:center;margin:24pt 0pt 0pt 0pt;">7</p></div></div></div>

style="font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;text-decoration-color:#000000;">PART&#160;I</b></p><a id="Item1Business_383443"></a><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Item&#160;1. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b style="font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;text-decoration-color:#000000;">Business</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Overview</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We are an independent oil and gas company engaged in development, production and acquisition activities primarily in the Rocky Mountains region of the United States where we are focused on developing our large resource play in the Williston Basin of North Dakota and Montana. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">On April&#160;1, 2020, we and certain of our subsidiaries (collectively, the &#8220;Debtors&#8221;) commenced voluntary cases (the &#8220;Chapter 11 Cases&#8221;) under chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code. &#160;On June&#160;30, 2020, the Debtors filed the Joint Chapter 11 Plan of Reorganization of Whiting Petroleum Corporation and its Debtor affiliates (as amended, modified, and supplemented, the &#8220;Plan&#8221;). &#160;On August&#160;14, 2020, the Bankruptcy Court confirmed the Plan and on September 1, 2020 (the &#8220;Emergence Date&#8221;), the Debtors satisfied all conditions required for Plan effectiveness and emerged from the Chapter 11 Cases. &#160;Upon emergence, we adopted fresh start accounting in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 852 &#8211; <i style="font-style:italic;">Reorganizations</i>, which specifies the accounting and financial reporting requirements for entities reorganizing through chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. &#160;The application of fresh start accounting resulted in a new basis of accounting and us becoming a new entity for financial reporting purposes. &#160;As a result of the implementation of the Plan and the application of fresh start accounting, the consolidated financial statements after the Emergence Date are not comparable to the consolidated financial statements before that date and the historical financial statements on or before the Emergence Date are not a reliable indicator of our financial condition and results of operations for any period after our adoption of fresh start accounting. &#160;Refer to the &#8220;Fresh Start Accounting&#8221; footnote in the consolidated financial statements in Item&#160;8 of this Annual Report on Form&#160;10-K for more information. &#160;References to &#8220;Successor&#8221; refer to the Whiting entity and its financial position and results of operations after the Emergence Date. &#160;References to &#8220;Predecessor&#8221; refer to the Whiting entity and its financial position and results of operations on or before the Emergence Date. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Since our inception, we have built a strong asset base through a combination of property acquisitions, development of proved reserves and exploration activities. &#160;Our current operations and capital programs are focused on drilling opportunities and on the development of previously acquired properties, specifically on projects that we believe provide the greatest potential for repeatable success, while selectively pursuing acquisitions that complement our existing core properties. &#160;As a result of the sharp decline in commodity prices during 2020 as well as our chapter 11 reorganization, we significantly reduced our level of capital spending during 2020 to more closely align with our reduced cash flows from operating activities. &#160;We concentrated our capital program on projects that we expect to generate acceptable rates of return in the current price environment. &#160;We continually evaluate our property portfolio and sell properties when we believe that the sales price realized will provide an above average rate of return for the property or when the property no longer matches the profile of properties we desire to own, such as the activity discussed below under &#8220;Acquisitions and Divestitures.&#8221;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, our estimated proved reserves totaled 260.2 MMBOE and our 2020 average daily production was 98.6 MBOE/d.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The following table summarizes by core area, our estimated proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2020 with the corresponding pre-tax PV10% values, our fourth quarter 2020 average daily production rates, style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:8pt;vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;">(2)</td><td style="padding:0pt;"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:justify;">Pre-tax PV10% may be considered a non-GAAP financial measure as defined by the SEC and is derived from the standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows (the &#8220;Standardized Measure&#8221;), which is the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure. &#160;Pre-tax PV10% is computed on the same basis as the Standardized Measure but without deducting future income taxes. &#160;We believe pre-tax PV10% is a useful measure for investors when evaluating the relative monetary significance of our oil and natural gas properties. &#160;We further believe investors may utilize our pre-tax PV10% as a basis for comparison of the relative size and value of our proved reserves to other companies because many factors that are unique to each individual company impact the amount of future income taxes to be paid. &#160;Our management uses this measure when assessing the potential return on investment related to our oil and gas properties and acquisitions. &#160;However, pre-tax PV10% is not a substitute for the Standardized Measure. &#160;Our pre-tax PV10% and Standardized 2020, we incurred $209 million in exploration and development (&#8220;E&amp;D&#8221;) expenditures, which consisted of $185 million incurred by the Predecessor and $24 million incurred by the Successor, and includes $208 million for the drilling and completion of 54 gross (30.4 net) wells. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Our current 2021 E&amp;D budget is a range of $228 million to $252 million, which we expect to fund with net cash provided by operating activities and cash on hand. &#160;Our level of E&amp;D expenditures is largely discretionary, although a portion of our E&amp;D expenditures are for non-operated properties where we have limited control over the timing and amount of such expenditures, and the amount of funds we devote to any particular activity may increase or decrease significantly depending on commodity prices, cash flows, available opportunities and development results, among other factors. &#160;To the extent net cash provided by operating activities is higher or lower than currently anticipated, we would generate more or less free cash flow than we currently anticipate, adjust our E&amp;D budget accordingly or adjust borrowings outstanding under our credit facility.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Acquisitions and Divestitures</p><p style="font-family:'Times New style="background-color:#ffffff;">In January 2020, we completed the divestiture of our interests in 30 non-operated, producing oil and gas wells and related undeveloped acreage located in McKenzie County, North Dakota for aggregate sales proceeds of $25 million (before closing adjustments). &#160;The divested properties consisted of less than 1% of our estimated proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2019 and 1% of our average daily production for the year ended December&#160;31, 2019.</span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New December&#160;31, 2020. </span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">2019 Acquisitions and Divestitures. &#160;</i>In July&#160;2019, we completed the divestiture of our interests in 137 non-operated, producing oil and gas wells located in McKenzie, Mountrail and Williams counties of North Dakota for aggregate sales proceeds of $27 million (before closing adjustments). &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">In August&#160;2019, we completed the divestiture of our interests in 58 non-operated, producing oil and gas wells located in Richland County, Montana and Mountrail and Williams counties of North Dakota for aggregate sales proceeds of $26 million (before closing adjustments).</p><p style="font-family:'Times New significant acquisitions during the year ended December&#160;31, 2019.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">2018 Acquisitions and Divestitures.</i> &#160;In July 2018, we completed the acquisition of approximately 54,800 net acres in the Williston Basin, including interests in 117 producing oil and gas wells and undeveloped acreage located in Richland County, Montana and McKenzie County, North Dakota for an aggregate purchase price of $130 million (before closing adjustments). &#160;The producing properties had estimated proved reserves of 25.7 MMBOE as of the acquisition date, 84% of which were crude oil and NGLs. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">There were no significant divestitures during the year ended December&#160;31, 2018. </p></div><div <div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;page-break-after:always;width:88.24%;border:0;margin:30pt 5.88% 30pt 5.88%;"></div><div style="max-width:100%;padding-left:5.88%;padding-right:5.88%;position:relative;"><div style="margin-top:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"><a href="#TOC"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;text-align:left;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Business Strategy</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Our goal is to generate meaningful growth in shareholder value through the development, production and acquisition of oil and gas projects with attractive rates of return on invested capital. &#160;Specifically, we have focused, and plan to continue to focus, on the following:</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Efficiently Developing and Producing our Existing Properties. &#160;</i>The development of our large resource play at our Williston Basin project in North Dakota and Montana continues to be our central objective. &#160;We have assembled approximately 729,700 gross (478,400 net) developed and undeveloped acres in this area. &#160;During 2020, we completed and brought online 46 gross (27.6 net) operated Bakken and Three Forks wells in the Williston Basin. &#160;As a result of the significant decline in crude oil prices in 2020, we suspended all drilling and completion activity and terminated our drilling rig contracts in April 2020. &#160;During the fourth quarter of 2020, we resumed completion activity, and in February 2021, we brought on a drilling rig. &#160;Under our current 2021 capital program, we expect to TIL approximately 56 gross (36.8 net) wells in this area during the year.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">At our Redtail field in the Denver-Julesburg Basin in Weld County, Colorado, we have assembled approximately 82,700 gross (71,600 net) developed and undeveloped acres. &#160;We completed and TIL 2 gross (1.9 net) wells in our Redtail field during 2020. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Disciplined Financial Approach. &#160;</i>Our goal is to remain financially strong, yet flexible, through the prudent management of our balance sheet and active management of our exposure to commodity price volatility. &#160;We have historically funded our acquisition and development activity through a combination of internally generated cash flows, equity and debt issuances, bank borrowings and certain oil and gas property divestitures, as appropriate, to maintain our financial position. &#160;As a result of the sharp decline in commodity prices during 2020 as well as our chapter 11 reorganization, we significantly reduced our level of capital spending and implemented various cost reduction measures during 2020 to more closely align our expenditures with our reduced cash flows from operating activities. &#160;We have concentrated our capital program on projects that we expect to generate acceptable rates of return in the current price environment. &#160;From time to time, we monetize non-core properties and use the net proceeds from these asset sales to repay debt under our credit agreement or fund our E&amp;D expenditures. &#160;For example, during 2020 and 2019 we sold certain oil and gas properties operated by third parties that no longer matched the profile of properties we desire to own. &#160;In addition, to support cash flow generation on our existing properties and help ensure expected cash flows from newly acquired properties, we periodically enter into derivative contracts. &#160;Typically, we use costless collars and swaps to provide an attractive base commodity price level. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Commitment to Safety and Social Responsibility. &#160;</i>We are committed to developing the resources the world needs in a safe and responsible way. &#160;We seek ways to better protect habitats and communities, find alternatives to freshwater use, reduce the lifecycle methane emissions of our operations and encourage waste reduction programs. &#160;Additionally, we are committed to transparency in reporting our environmental, social and governance performance. &#160;See our Sustainability Report published on our website for sustainability performance highlights and additional information.&#160; Information contained in our Sustainability Report is not incorporated by reference into, and does not constitute a part of, this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Growing Through Accretive Acquisitions. &#160;</i>Since 2010, we have completed 7 separate significant acquisitions of producing properties for total estimated proved reserves of 240.2 MMBOE, as of the effective dates of the acquisitions. &#160;Our experienced team of management, land, engineering and geoscience professionals has executed an acquisition program designed to increase reserves and complement our existing properties, including closing purchases and effectively managing the properties we acquire. &#160;We intend to selectively pursue the acquisition of properties that are complementary to our core operating areas, as well as explore opportunities in other basins where we can apply our existing knowledge and expertise to build production and add proved reserves.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><b style="font-weight:bold;">Competitive Strengths</b></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We believe that our key competitive strengths lie in our focused asset portfolio, our experienced management and technical teams, our commitment to the effective application of new technologies and our commitment to cost management.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Focused, Long-Lived Asset Base</i>.<i style="font-style:italic;"> &#160;</i>As of December&#160;31, 2020, we had interests in 5,011 gross (2,175 net) productive wells on approximately 856,900 gross (567,000 net) developed acres across our geographical areas. &#160;We believe the concentration of our operated assets presents us with multiple opportunities to successfully execute our business strategy by enabling us to leverage our technical expertise and take advantage of operational efficiencies. </p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Experienced Management and Technical Teams</i>.<i style="font-style:italic;"> &#160;</i>Our management team averages 24 years of experience in the oil and gas industry. &#160;Our personnel have extensive experience in our core geographical areas, all of our operational disciplines and the evaluation, acquisition and operational assimilation of oil and gas properties.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Commitment to Technology</i>.<i style="font-style:italic;"> &#160;</i>In each of our core operating areas, we have accumulated extensive engineering, operational, geologic and geophysical technical knowledge. &#160;Our technical team has access to an abundance of digital well log, seismic, completion, production and other subsurface information, which is analyzed in order to accurately and efficiently characterize the anticipated performance of </p></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New databases through field automation. &#160;This commitment to technology has increased the productivity and efficiency of our field operations and development activities. &#160;Administratively, we have leveraged information systems to reduce duplications of data which has increased information reliability and minimized redundant processes.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We continue to advance our completion techniques by utilizing custom, right-sized completion designs based on calibrated models for each of our prospect areas, incorporating multivariate analysis and piloting and adopting the latest completion technologies available. &#160;Our multivariate analysis workflow leverages public and proprietary data to solve for production and cost, using those results to optimize well design details for maximum asset value. &#160;We plan to continue to use right-sized completion designs on wells we drill in 2021 and to expand our application of data analytics and multivariate analysis to unlock value across the business. &#160;Additionally, we plan to continue to reduce time-on-location and total well cost while maximizing our lateral footage through drilling best practices including utilizing top tier drilling rigs, advanced downhole motor and drill bit technology and our custom drilling fluid system.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="font-style:italic;">Commitment to Cost Management. &#160;</i>We are committed to cost reduction strategies to become a lower-cost basin operator. &#160;As a result of the sharp decline in commodity prices during 2020 as well as our chapter 11 reorganization, we significantly reduced our operating and overhead costs during 2020. &#160;In September 2020 and August 2019, we executed workforce reductions as part of our organizational redesign and cost reduction strategies to better align our business with the current operating environment. &#160;During 2020, we reduced lease operating expenses across all of our properties and maintained base production with improved artificial lift techniques and targeted workovers. &#160;These cost reduction and production maintenance efforts resulted in reducing saltwater disposal costs by 40%, extending well runtimes by 7.5% and reducing down oil volume by 35% from year-end 2019 to year-end 2020. &#160;</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We expect that our ongoing cost management efforts will result in sustainable operations and long-term value to our shareholders.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Proved Reserves</p><p of Contents</span></a></p></div><div style="clear:both;max-width:100%;position:relative;"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Marketing</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We principally sell our oil and gas production to end users, marketers and other purchasers that have access to nearby pipeline or rail takeaway. &#160;In areas where there is no practical access to gathering pipelines, oil is trucked or transported to terminals, market hubs, refineries or storage facilities. &#160;We believe that the loss of any individual purchaser would not have a long-term material adverse impact on our financial position or results of operations, as alternative customers and markets for the sale of our products are readily available in the areas in which we operate.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:12pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Title to Properties</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Our properties are subject to customary royalty interests, liens securing indebtedness, liens incident to operating agreements, liens for current taxes and other burdens, including other mineral encumbrances and restrictions. &#160;Our credit agreement is also collateralized by a first lien on substantially all of our assets. &#160;We do not believe that any of these burdens materially interfere with the use of our properties or the operation of our business.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We believe that we have satisfactory rights or title to all of our producing properties. &#160;As is customary in the oil and gas industry, limited investigation of title is made at the time of acquisition of undeveloped properties. &#160;In most cases, we investigate title and obtain title opinions from counsel only when we acquire producing properties or before commencement of drilling operations.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Competition</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">The oil and gas industry is a highly competitive environment for acquiring properties, obtaining investment capital, securing oil field goods and services, marketing oil and natural gas products and attracting and retaining qualified personnel. &#160;Many of our competitors possess and employ financial, technical and personnel resources substantially greater than ours, which can be particularly important in the areas in which we operate. &#160;Those companies may be able to pay more for productive oil and gas properties and exploratory prospects and to evaluate, bid for and purchase a greater number of properties and prospects than our resources permit. &#160;In addition, the unavailability or high cost of drilling rigs, completion crews or other equipment and services could delay or adversely affect our development and exploration operations. &#160;Our ability to acquire additional prospects and to find and develop reserves in the future will depend on our ability to obtain necessary capital as well as evaluate and select suitable properties and to consummate transactions in a highly competitive environment.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">In addition, the oil and gas industry as a whole competes with other industries in supplying the energy and fuel requirements of industrial, commercial and individual consumers. &#160;The price and availability of alternative energy sources, such as wind, solar, nuclear and electric power, as well as the emerging impact of climate change activism, fuel conservation measures and governmental requirements for renewable energy sources, could adversely affect our revenue.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">Human Capital</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;">We believe that in order to execute our strategy in the highly competitive oil and gas industry we need to attract, develop and retain a highly effective and diverse employee workforce. &#160;<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Our ability to do so ties to a number of factors, including compensation plans, benefits programs, talent development efforts, career opportunity generation and our work environment. &#160;A</span>s of January&#160;31, 2021, we had approximately 405 full-time employees, 245 of which were field employees and none of which were represented by any labor unions.</p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="background-color:#ffffff;font-style:italic;">Competitive Compensation and Benefits.</i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> &#160;The objective of our compensation program is to maintain a strong pay-for-performance culture in order to attract, retain and motivate employees. &#160;Our program includes competitive market-based salaries, short-term incentives that tie to corporate and individual performance, long-term incentives and market-competitive health and other benefits. </span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="background-color:#ffffff;font-style:italic;">Training, Development and Career Opportunities. </i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> We are committed to the personal and professional development of our employees, with the belief that a greater level of knowledge, skill and ability is of personal benefit to the employee and fosters a more creative, innovative, efficient and therefore competitive company. &#160;We strive to empower our employees to develop the skills they need to perform their current jobs while developing acumen for future opportunities. &#160;We want our talent pool to identify a successful and fulfilling career progression within our company. </span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 0pt;"><i style="background-color:#ffffff;font-style:italic;">Diversity, Equity and Inclusion</i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">. &#160;We recognize the advantages of a company culture that embraces diversity, constructive debate and differing viewpoints. &#160;We believe that a workforce diverse in background and experience will create such a culture. &#160;We recruit, hire, promote and perform personnel actions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information or any other applicable status by federal, state or local law. </span></p><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i style="background-color:#ffffff;font-style:italic;">Safety. &#160;</i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#8220;Safety Always&#8221; is one of our core, foundational values. &#160;We strive to create a culture of safety that promotes transparency and accountability by providing the tools and resources that empower our people to identify and report potential hazards and stop work when </span></p></div><div style="clear:both;display:table;margin-bottom:14.4pt;min-height:21.6pt;width:100%;"><div style="display:table-cell;vertical-align:bottom;width:100%;"><p style="font-family:'Times New
